title: A gate failure surfaces the failing gate and its report path in the operator-visible output
asA: reviewer whose first look at a red CI job is the runner-log tail
iWant: the tail of the failing pipeline job to name the failing gate and point me at the report file
soThat: I find the detail I need without clicking through the provider's UI

acceptanceCriteria.description: On any gate failure, the Node entry point writes an operator-readable failure summary to its own stderr naming the failing gate, its exit code, and the relative path to the per-gate report file.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an invocation of the suite whose `validate` (or any) gate fails
acceptanceCriteria.when: the reviewer reads the runner-log tail (the Node process's own stderr)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the tail contains a single-line summary matching the shape `[ci-pipeline] gate '<gate>' failed (exit <n>); report: <reportDir>/<gate>.json`, and the reference report file exists at the named path

acceptanceCriteria.description: The suite continues past a failing gate to run the remaining required gates and record their outcomes. Multiple gate failures produce multiple entries in the aggregate report's `gates[]` array, each carrying its own outcome and report path.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a suite invocation against a tree that fails both `validate` and `coverage-strict`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the aggregate report's `gates[]` array contains both `validate` and `coverage-strict` entries, each with `outcome: failed`, and each with a `reportPath` value pointing to an existing per-gate report file
